text:
Morgan Geekie arrived at this season off a 39-goal year in Boston, and for a while it looked like the scoring had stayed behind. Then came a four-goal streak in early November, capped by a power-play goal in the 4-1 win over Florida, and a new second line with Mikey Eyssimont. He has 15 points in 20 games, eight of them on the power play.

The shooting is not the issue. He has five goals on 5.9 expected (expected goals measure the quality of his chances), and his shot is still one of the hardest in the league, 99th percentile by NHL Edge. The worry is the even-strength picture: the Bruins take 45.6% of the shot attempts with him on the ice at five on five, and they do noticeably worse with him out there than without him. His team has also scored 4.7 more goals than expected while he plays, which flatters his assists.

His minutes have slipped by two and a half a night over the last ten, and he has gone three games without a shot. Evolving-Hockey had him as a better player than his goals last season. Watch whether the second line keeps its shape.
headline: Geekie's goals came back, the five-on-five didn't
